title: Add per-IP rate limiting to the auth endpoints
subtitle: Protect /login and /reset from brute-force and quota exhaustion
summary: Login and password-reset are currently unthrottled. A scripted client can brute-force credentials or burn our email-provider quota. **Plan:** add a small token-bucket limiter on the existing Redis client, applied per-route via a decorator, returning `429` with `Retry-After`. First cut covers `/login` and `/reset`; configurable limits are deferred.

items.title: Add token-bucket limiter
items.md: Atomic decrement via a Redis Lua script so concurrent requests can't race the bucket.

blocks.note: An **editable + runnable** snippet so reviewers can poke at the limiter logic inside the plan itself.

blocks.rationale: The API runs multiple workers, so an **in-process** counter would let each worker grant its own quota. Redis is already a dependency. Gateway throttling can't see per-account limits we'll want later.

items.q: Make limits configurable before prod, or hardcode 5/min for the first cut?
items.recommendation: hardcode now, env var in follow-up
